summary: Colville NF tower near Republic, Ferry County WA: built 1933, L-4 moved in from Churchill Mtn 1955, cut to 30 ft 1959, burned by arson Oct 1997.

facts.design: 40-foot pole L-4 built 1933 per the register; a 53-foot L-4 moved in from Churchill Mountain in 1955; cut to 30 feet and given a flat R-6 cab in 1959
facts.status_note: The cabin and 30-foot tower burned to the ground in October 1997; the cause was arson

staffing.status: Fire detection season ended 1977 per the Washington Lookouts page; known personnel listed 1945 to 1959

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Colville National Forest

events.note: Register says a 40-foot pole L-4 was built in 1933. Republic items from September 1932 and July 1933 describe raising and completing a tower.
Road to the lookout completed; garage and storehouse built at its end for the fire-season lookout
Listed as activated May 9, 1942 and deactivated July 1, 1943, under the Seattle Filter Center; no further detail given
Known lookout personnel listed from 1945 through 1959, including Alwilda Webb (1945) and Tom Windsor (1959)
53-foot L-4 tower moved to Quartz from Churchill Mountain
L-4 cab removed, tower trimmed to 30 feet, flat R-6 cab affixed to the top
Last season the lookout was used for fire detection; register says it was abandoned in the 1970s and then vandalized
Cabin and 30-foot tower burned to the ground on October 7, 1997; Colville National Forest officials said arson
Registered November 18, 2012 as US 1460, WA 360, nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) is the height of the original 1933 pole tower. The register says the tower was trimmed to 30 feet in 1959, and the 1997 newspaper item describes a 30-foot tower when it burned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Early height varies: the register says a 40-foot pole (1933); a July 1933 item says about 50 feet; a 1935 item says 40 feet. The register and the 1997 item both give 30 feet for the final tower, which the record uses.
The register gives 4,799 ft (1,463 m); the 1997 item gives 4,830 feet. The story and the record use the register figure.
The register dates the build to 1933; a September 1932 item says a tower was being raised that year. The story says the tower went up in 1932 or 1933.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 12.2 is the 1933 pole height; corrected to 9.1 (30 ft), the height when the tower was trimmed and when it burned. Access is unknown in the brief and no source states it, so it is left out. The Seattle Filter Center line is unexplained on its page and is included only as the page states it. Not read: the Churchill Mountain Facebook post, the Republic News-Miner and Six Twenty-Six originals. Do not confuse with Quartz Mountain in Kittitas County (FFLOS US 1378, tower gone) or Quartz Mountain (Relocated Mount Spokane, US 1558, standing), both listed on firelookout.org.
